answers.rationale: Use a taxi from PHL and walk locally. All activity is downtown, materials are sponsor-handled, and normal luggage does not justify downtown rental, parking, or daily-car friction. History shows car use is conditional on equipment and multi-site travel rather than a fixed transportation preference.

Use the client-campus hotel for the advisory, then move downtown when Mark joins. The work and leisure portions have different location needs, and no equipment removes the main operational downside of a move. History supports split stays only when their concrete benefit is real, not as a fixed habit; exact campus-to-downtown travel time could change the recommendation.

Stay office-adjacent for the daytime work sessions, then move waterfront for the designated recovery day. With no cartons or hotel receiving, the move is operationally manageable and gives the recovery day a distinct benefit. Prior history shows both continuous and split stays depending on the agenda, so there is no fixed lodging-location preference.

Keep one waterfront downtown reservation for all nights. Vendor-supplied equipment removes the need to stay office-adjacent for gear handling, and a single downtown base best preserves the Saturday leisure day without a hotel move. The vendor-office commute and rate difference are unspecified, so this remains context-sensitive rather than a stable preference.
